name: ROADtools (ROADrecon)
what: A framework for Entra ID (Azure AD) exploration. ROADrecon authenticates to Microsoft Graph, stores a tenant snapshot locally, and serves an HTML interface so red and blue teams can inspect users, apps, roles and relationships without clicking through the portal all day.
when: During Entra-focused assessments or continuous purple-team reviews when you need an offline, queryable picture of directory objects, app permissions and privileged roles.
example: Install ROADrecon from PyPI into a virtualenv on an admin workstation: `pip install roadrecon`.
Authenticate with an account that has agreed Graph read permissions and gather: `roadrecon auth` then `roadrecon gather`.
Start the GUI against the local database: `roadrecon gui`, and review high-privilege roles, stale guests and over-permissioned apps.
Export findings into tickets; re-gather after remediation to show the diff.
pitfalls: Gathered data is a full tenant map; protect the database like production identity exports.
Permissions that are too broad for the test account create lasting risk; use least privilege and revoke after the test.
ROADtools is not a substitute for Conditional Access and identity governance reviews; combine with Maester or ScubaGear.
